subject.title: fix(firecrawl,brave,web-search,web-fetch,models-config): use own-property checks for config field lookups

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally reject inherited fields on all programmatically supplied config and model objects even though no supported external ingestion path currently demonstrates this state?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but accepting its broad compatibility change depends on whether maintainers consider inherited-field behavior unsupported defense-in-depth or want the change narrowed to a proven trust boundary.

options.title: Prove and narrow first
options.body: Require current-head supported-path evidence and retain only substitutions protecting a reachable trust boundary, while adopting the dynamic Firecrawl test inventory.

options.title: Accept own-only semantics
options.body: Declare inherited fields unsupported for programmatic config/model objects and accept the broader compatibility change with a proof override and test-hunk reconciliation.

options.title: Pause the hardening
options.body: Pause or close the PR if no supported path can produce prototype-bearing inputs and the defense-in-depth value does not justify the added test surface.

recommendation.title: Prove and narrow first
recommendation.body: Require current-head supported-path evidence and retain only substitutions protecting a reachable trust boundary, while adopting the dynamic Firecrawl test inventory.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work localized the Brave provider and implemented central web-provider selection behavior, giving this owner the strongest cross-surface context for the compatibility boundary.
